title: provisioning matrix: tokens-qps and gpu-pool sizing 2026-q2
content:
Purpose:
This working sheet defines a provisioning matrix for Hosted API peak demand across regions and GPU pool types. It focuses on tokens/sec and QPS projections for near-term (12 week) runway and defines headroom targets and actionable triggers for reserved capacity and temporary burst allocations. The goal is to keep 99th percentile tail latency SLAs while minimizing waste.

Executive summary (one-liner):
Baseline global 99th-percentile peak projected at ~1.8M tokens/sec (mid-May worst-day estimate) with regional concentrations in US-W/US-E and EU-W. Target operational headroom: 40% on regional pools and 25% on global routing buffer to absorb traffic delta and model rollouts.

Assumptions (explicit):
- Baseline traffic window: 08:00-20:00 local; global peak dominated by US business hours.
- Tokenization: avg tokens per request = 230 (chat mix).
- Avg QPS per token burst approximated by tokens/sec / avg tokens.
- Model mix: 55% lower-quantized L4-like (cheaper), 30% A100-optimized, 15% H100/long-context variants.
- Expected growth: conservative +2.8% weekly linear (feature launches + marketing).
- Failure modes: regional AZ outage, model rollout regressions, sudden traffic spikes from partner integrations.

Scenarios defined:
- Baseline peak (P50->P95 steady growth): projections assume normal growth and one marketing spike per quarter.
- Stress spike (P99.5): simultaneous partner launches + weekday holiday effect -> multiply baseline tokens/sec by 1.6.
- Release regression: a bad rollout increases average token usage by +20% for 6-12 hours.
- Region outage reroute: 100% of region traffic falls back to other regions; routing capacity must accommodate 1.2x traffic in remaining regions for at least 4 hours.

Provisioning matrix (summary table):
Columns: region | current provisioned tokens/sec | projected peak tokens/sec (12w P99) | headroom target (%) | target provisioned tokens/sec | dominant gpu pool type | target pool size (gpus)
US-W | 520,000 | 720,000 | 40 | 1,008,000 | A100-80GB + L4 mix | 84 x A100 equiv
US-E | 460,000 | 640,000 | 40 | 896,000 | H100 (long tail) + L4 | 72 x A100 equiv
EU-W | 360,000 | 500,000 | 40 | 700,000 | A100-heavy | 56 x A100 equiv
AP-S | 160,000 | 220,000 | 40 | 308,000 | L4 + small H100 reserve | 24 x A100 equiv
LATAM | 80,000 | 110,000 | 40 | 154,000 | L4 | 12 x A100 equiv
Global routing buffer | N/A | N/A | 25 | 450,000 (buffer capacity) | mixed | N/A
Notes on table conversions: A100-equivalent sizing is a rough normalized unit (1 A100-80GB = 1.0 eq). L4 instances normalized as 0.15 A100-eq, H100 as 1.3 A100-eq for long-context models. Exact GPU counts to be reconciled with vendor SKU inventories.

Utilization targets and SLOs:
- Operational target utilization per pool: 55-68% steady-state.
- Alert threshold (auto-scaling required): sustained 72% for 2 hours or 85% for 15 minutes.
- Safety ceiling: do not exceed 90% sustained for >5 minutes without emergency scaling.

Buffering strategy and placement priorities:
1) Local headroom (40%): scale regional pools first to minimize cross-region latency and egress costs.
2) Global routing buffer (25%): ephemeral capacity in a neutral region (US-Central/neutral zone) used only when cross-region capacity exhausted.
3) Model fallbacks: when A100/H100 capacity constrained, route to quantized variants on L4 when latency budget allows.

Scaling policy (practical triggers):
- Autoscale up: add burst nodes when 5-minute rolling tokens/sec exceeds 80% of configured target_provisioned_tokens for the pool and prediction model indicates >10% increase in next hour.
- Manual provisioning trigger: sustained alert (util >72%) + on-call approval -> order temporary reserved instances (48-72 hr lead) or activate cloud burst credits.
- Rollback trigger: if latency regression > 30% after a model rollout or cost per token > projected threshold for >4 hours, revert to previous model and increase headroom by +10% immediately.

Lead times and procurement notes:
- Pre-provision reserved capacity (quarterly commit) average lead time: 2-4 weeks for enterprise reservations; plan commits 6 weeks ahead of predicted seasonal peaks.
- Spot/ephemeral capacity: immediate, but plan for 25% preemption risk—do not use for critical low-latency workloads.
- On-call ops playbook for emergency purchases: Ops runbook ID JIRA-OPS-4912.

Cost optimization levers (short list):
- Shift non-latency-critical inference to quantized L4 pools during off-peak to lower unit cost.
- Encourage developers to pin shorter contexts and use streaming to reduce peak token concurrency.
- Autoscaler tuning: widen batch window by +10ms for low-latency-tolerant routes to improve packing and reduce effective GPUs.

Open questions / follow-ups (action items):
- Validate normalized A100-equivalent conversions against vendor telemetry (action: Ethan Park, due 2026-03-10).
- Run a synthetic P99.5 stress test targeting 1.6x baseline for 3 hours in staging and capture routing fallback behavior (action: Rhea Singh, test run week of 2026-03-08).
- Confirm lead times for reserved A100 and H100 SKUs with cloud account team (action: Marisol Chen, due 2026-03-05).

Appendix A — quick math examples:
- Example: US-W projected peak tokens/sec = 720k; with 40% headroom target -> provision = 720k * 1.4 = 1,008,000 tokens/sec. If an A100-equivalent can sustain ~12,000 tokens/sec at target-latency, target pool = 1,008,000 / 12,000 = 84 A100-eq.
- Example stress: P99.5 global spike = 1.8M * 1.6 = 2.88M tokens/sec; with global buffers + local headroom we aim to absorb 75% of that without emergency throttling; required ephemeral capacity = (2.88M - absorbed_by_local) estimate -> see stress runbook.

Doc history and context:
- This sheet replaces earlier ad-hoc runbooks and consolidates the provisioning matrix into region-first headroom targets and a global routing buffer. It is intended to be a working artifact; numbers will be updated weekly during capacity planning syncs.
- Related docs: hosted-api-peak-scaling-playbook-q3-2026 (reference), capacity-runway-tokens-qps-by-region-2026q2 (reference).
